profile.name: Honey's Mini Therapy Adventures
profile.description:
We are a portable equine therapy program. We visit Hospital campuses across Central Florida every week. We also provide k-12 schools and colleges. In addition to inpatient behavioral and mental health campuses. 
     The benefits of equine therapy are well known. We quickly realized the immeasurable need for this amazing service in our community. Especially in the healthcare/clinical setting as it relates to mental health. Equine therapy is effective alongside a variety of medical and psychological conditions. People with P.T.S.D., anxiety, depression, and autism benefit from a therapeutic relationship and alliance the horses help form and provide. There isn't a population we have crossed paths with yet, no age, gender, ethnicity, sexual orientation, or socioeconomic class that does not benefit from the unique therapy these tiny horses provide within so many different settings.
Powered with @streamhorsetv

videos.description: POV: The therapy horse who literally doesn’t care… She’s just here to make everyone SMILE 🤣🐴 Hospital day = Dumpling being the main character and is all smiles #IDontCare #SmilingHorse #MiniTherapyHorse #fyp #pov

💛 Healing Happens at Any Age 💛 When our miniature therapy horses visit senior care communities, something truly special happens. 📊 Based on our post-visit data, families and staff consistently report: 🐴 Smiling and laughter 🧠 Reduced anxiety and agitation 🗣️ Increased social interaction 💭 Memories sparked from long ago 💛 Improved overall mood and emotional well-being Families rated these visits as “Extremely meaningful,” with an average well-being impact of nearly 5 out of 5. One family shared: “The gentleness of the pony brought such a calm and peaceful feeling.” For many seniors, especially those living with dementia or Alzheimer’s, the presence of a horse isn’t just comforting — it reconnects them to memories, emotions, and moments they thought were lost. 🐴💫 This is why we do what we do. Because healing, connection, and joy don’t have an age limit. 💬 Have you seen the power of animals with seniors? Tell us below. #SeniorCare #MemoryCare #DementiaCare #HealingWithHorses #MiniTherapyHorses

They don’t speak. They don’t judge. But somehow… they always know. Tag someone who’s ever been healed by a horse. #HorseTok #EquineTherapy #MiniMiracles #HealingWithHorses #HorseLovers #EmotionalSupport #HorseMagic #TherapyHorse #YouAreSeen #UnspokenComfort

Can’t wait to pick up Ten LS Lucinda at Nationals this year! 🤍 Our AMHA/AMHR/ASPC Kentucky Incentive 2025 filly is such a pretty little mover, and we’re so excited to finally bring her home. There’s just something special about this filly. ✨🐴 Nationals can’t get here fast enough!

😂 Miniature show horse or bronc? Jury’s still out. Sassy got all scrubbed, cleaned up, and ready to show… and apparently decided that was the perfect time to turn her stall into a rodeo arena. 🤦🏼‍♀️😂 Spinning around like a helicopter, feeling herself, and making sure we remembered that underneath all that pretty is a whole lotta SASS. 💅🏼🐴 Nothing says show ready quite like immediately trying to undo all the work. 😂  #SassyGirl #MiniatureHorse #ShowHorse #TinyButMighty @Cheyenne

POV: You tell your miniature horse it’s just a little hair dye… and he comes out looking like he’s about to drop the hottest emo album of 2006. 🖤😂🐴 We dyed Wyatt’s mane and apparently unlocked an entirely new personality. The wet hair-dye phase was questionable… the dry reveal was giving ✨tiny emo heartthrob✨… and then he hitched up to the cart like, “Yeah, I look good. Drive on.” 😂 The HAIR. The ATTITUDE. The tiny little legs. I cannot handle him. 🖤 It’s not a phase, Mom. 🖤🐴😂 #MiniatureHorse #MiniHorse #EmoHorse #ItsNotAPhaseMom #HorseTok

Mud season is in full swing on the farm… and Doc and Wyatt have fully embraced the lifestyle. 🤦🏼‍♀️😂 One good rainstorm and somehow our beautiful horses transform into swamp creatures overnight. Doc was especially proud of his accomplishment. 💀 Today’s agenda looked something like this: 🤎 Catch the muddy horses. 🛁 Give Doc an antifungal spa day to stay ahead of summer skin issues. 🐴 Round pen work with Cheyenne to help him learn to use his body more efficiently in the cart. ☀️ Let him dry. 🙃 Turn him back out… …and if you know Doc, you already know what happened next. The very first thing he’ll do is find the biggest mud puddle on the farm and roll like his life depends on it. 😂 Between the Florida heat, humidity, bugs, and mud, keeping everyone healthy takes a lot of work this time of year. Every bath, every treatment, every training session is another small investment in keeping these horses feeling their best so they can continue changing lives through our therapy program. Now who’s next? 🙋🏼‍♀️ Betty White and Violet… your spa appointments are officially on the schedule. 🧼💕 #MiniTherapyHorse #FarmLife #HorseLife #MiniatureHorse #BehindTheScenes

Early in my career as a hospital social worker, I met a survivor of human trafficking. I remember thinking, “They don’t look like someone who’s been trafficked.” That moment changed me. The truth is, trafficking doesn’t have one face. It lives all around us, often hidden in plain sight. Today, as an LCSW, I had the privilege of leading our very first equine-facilitated psychotherapy group for survivors of human trafficking. We combined CBT, DBT, and Motivational Interviewing, but it was our miniature therapy horses, Wyatt and Sugarfoot, who quietly reminded everyone what safety feels like. Our message was simple: You are worthy. You are not what you’ve been through. Some days remind you exactly why you chose your profession. For me, it’s to be a light in the darkness for others until they begin to see the light within themselves. 🤍🐴 #HumanTraffickingAwareness #TraumaRecovery #LCSW #TherapyHorse #EquineTherapy

Sometimes healing walks through the hospital doors on four tiny hooves. 🐴🤍 Therapy horses can offer a moment of calm in the middle of uncertainty—helping reduce stress and anxiety, encouraging connection, lifting spirits, and giving patients, families, and healthcare teams something positive to focus on. For a few moments, the hospital room feels a little less clinical. There are smiles. Laughter. Connection. And sometimes, simply a quiet moment of peace. Our horses may be small, but the comfort they carry is immeasurable. 🤍🐴 #TherapyHorses #MiniatureHorses #HospitalTherapy #MentalHealthMatters #HorsesHealingHearts

Some of the most important places our horses will ever visit… you’ll never see. This month, Honey’s Mini Therapy Adventures begins one of the most meaningful missions we’ve ever been called to. Twice each month, our miniature therapy horses will visit survivors of human trafficking at an undisclosed location. For their safety and privacy, we won’t share photos, videos, or where these visits take place. Some stories aren’t ours to tell. What we can share is why it matters. Trauma can make the world feel unsafe. Horses have an incredible ability to meet people without judgment, fear, or expectations. A gentle nuzzle, a quiet moment, or simply standing beside them can help survivors feel calm, connected, and reminded that kindness still exists. Our mission has always been to be a light in the darkness. Whether we’re visiting children in hospitals, supporting first responders, walking alongside those struggling with mental health, or now serving survivors of human trafficking, our purpose remains the same: to bring hope, healing, and connection—one heart at a time. Some of our most important work will never go viral. And we’re okay with that. ❤️🐴 #TherapyHorses #HumanTraffickingAwareness #TraumaHealing #mentalhealth
Doc the Hippo, Pearl the Zebra, and Rocket the Leopard with their ZooKeeper 🦛 🐆 🦓  #amhaproud #amhya #amhayouth

🐴✨ Horse Lesson Saturday = Core Memories Made ✨🐴 Cheyenne and Faith came over today and we had an absolute BLAST! 💛 ✔️ Worked on driving ✔️ Tackled driving obstacle ✔️ Rode to the country store (because nothing beats real-world desensitizing!) ✔️ Explored the back 8 acres ✔️ Practiced showmanship ✔️ Loaded the trailer to get ready for our upcoming shows Somewhere between all the laughs and horse hair, Cheyenne looked around the back pasture and said… “There’s plenty of room for more ponies back here.” 😂 Listen… we don’t need that kind of encouragement. 🤣🐴 Days like this remind us that horse showing isn’t just about ribbons—it’s about friendships, adventures, confidence, and making memories with the people and horses we love. Now the trailer is loaded, the horses are ready, and we’re counting down the days to Kentucky, Gainesville, and Georgia! ❤️✨ it’s gunna be a busy 3 weeks.  Anyone else have that one horse friend who is a terrible influence when it comes to buying more horses? 🙋‍♀️😂 #HorseGirlProblems #MiniHorseLife #HorseShowLife #DrivingHorse #HorseTraining @Cheyenne @Faith Kopycinski

🐴💜 Violet’s Story 💜🐴 I almost didn’t share this. Partly because it’s been emotional to relive, and partly because I think I needed time before I could look at her without reliving those moments all over again. But after watching Violet walk into the show ring this week… I realized her story deserved to be told. When we brought Violet home in March, she was young, scared, and unsure of us. Everything was new to her, and like a lot of young horses, fear came before trust. Less than a week later, we had a freak accident that changed everything in seconds. She hit a fence. Hard. I still remember the sound. I remember Autumn crying beside me while I stood there in complete panic calling our vet, trying to stay calm for both of them. I remember looking at Violet and genuinely thinking, “There is no way this horse survives this.” In that moment, I truly thought we were going to lose her. The next day we took her to Equine Medical Center Ocala, where ultrasounds and X-rays confirmed nerve damage and Sweeney Shoulder. The prognosis came with no guarantees. Maybe she’d recover. Maybe partially. Maybe not at all. For weeks, our lives revolved around rehab. Medications. Stall rest. PEMF therapy. Laser treatments. Tiny signs of progress that felt huge to us. But honestly, one of the hardest parts wasn’t the injury itself… it was the emotional rollercoaster afterward. Some days she looked stronger and we’d feel hopeful again, only for her to suddenly seem sore or weaker the next day. Recovery wasn’t linear for Violet. It came with setbacks, fear, hope, exhaustion, and so many unknowns. Some nights I prayed she’d make it back to the show ring someday. Some nights I hoped maybe she could still have babies one day, even if she never showed again. And some nights, sitting beside her stall, my prayers became much simpler: That she’d just walk comfortably again and have a happy life. Somewhere through all the treatments, long nights, and rehab… something changed between us too. The scared horse that didn’t trust us when she first arrived now follows me everywhere. She waits for me at the gate. She walks behind me like my little shadow. We built trust through healing. And this week, when she walked into the show ring, I had tears in my eyes before the class even started… because three months ago, I wasn’t dreaming about this moment anymore. I was simply praying she’d have a good quality of life. Thank you to every single person who helped us through this — our veterinarians, specialists, friends, horse people, and everyone who prayed for her or answered frantic late-night phone calls. Violet has taught me that healing isn’t always quick, pretty, or guaranteed… but sometimes hope is enough to keep going. 💜 #sweenyshoulder #horseinjury #recoveryjourney #equinetherapy #horsesoftiktok

top of pageHomeAboutOur HorsesOur TeamContactMoreUse tab to navigate through the menu items.DONATE SPONSOR AN ADVENTUREDid you know your organization can sponsor a Honey's Mini Therapy Adventure? We are opening up the opportunity for aligning organizations to partner with us on visits. Click below to view our 2024 Sponsorship Opportunities. Sponsorship Opportunites Call 813-957-3322Email honey@minitherapy.orgFollowAre You Interested in Volunteering?Honey's Mini Therapy Adventures is looking for qualified volunteers to join our program. Whether you have experience with horses, mental health, or administrative work, we are accepting volunteers in all aspects who are a good fit for our organization. ​ Please fill out our volunteer application form to join our team!Volunteer Form WHAT PEOPLE SAY"Banyan Pediatric Care Centers, a medical daycare facility, has been honored to partner with Honey’s Mini Therapy Adventures for a year now. We initially believed their visit would be a one-time treat, as they had to travel over an hour to get to us, and we operate from a very limited budget. But because of their kindness, and the noticeable impact their visit had on our kids, they were determined to find a way to maintain a relationship. Eventually, they secured funding to make visits twice a month across all THREE of our locations! They travel hours back and forth to fulfill their mission of improving others’ quality of life. These visits bring both our children and staff so much joy, and we consider them a vital part of the Banyan experience. Our children all have medically-complex diagnoses, some with limited mobility, disregulated sensory systems, behavioral issues, and other disabilities that would otherwise make interactions with animals difficult, or impossible. Honey’s gives our children an opportunity to have an entirely novel experience, regulate their emotions, calm their anxieties, and receive unconditional love from a furry friend. Both the handlers and their horses are equally patient, kind, and selfless for what they do. With increased funding and donations, they can continue to spread their joy to facilities like ours and beyond." ​ Banyan Pediatrics Care Centers, 2023 Have You Been with us on a Recent Visit?Please take a minute to fill out our post-visit questionnaire to help our research study with The University of Tampa. pages.title: About | Honey's Mini Therapy Adventures
pages.excerpt:
top of pageHomeAboutOur HorsesOur TeamContactMoreUse tab to navigate through the menu items.DONATE OUR MISSION Honey's Mini Therapy Adventures is a 501c3 nonprofit organization that brings therapy horses to many Central Florida facilities. We visit Tampa General Hospital, Saint Leo University, Pasco Hernando State College, University of Central Florida. In addition to these organizations, we visit smaller nursing homes and local schools weekly. ​ In 2018 we began our work & quickly realized how Honey & our therapy horses were affecting dementia and Alzheimer's patients. The horses' smells, sight, and touch bring back long-forgotten memories. It is incredible to see and be a part of such a unique service that genuinely makes a ripple effect impact on the facilities we visit. Dementia/Autism/Cancer not only affects the individual themselves but is so hard on the family members and caretakers that love them. ​ ​ Our visits also impact the staff; everyone from patients to guests responds positively to the tiny horses. For example, in our most recent Tampa General Hospital visit, we were told numerous times, "This little, tiny horse just made my entire day; You have no idea how much I needed this." Another staff member states, "All her anxiety and stress literally washed away." If the tiny horse positively impacts someone's day that we crossed paths within a hospital, then it's worth all the hard work that goes in behind the scenes to facilitate our therapy visits. ​ ​So many different populations/backgrounds and ages can benefit from the unique service our handlers and tiny horses provide. These horses may be miniature, but their impact on the community we serve is tremendous.WHO WE SERVEWe serve a variety of facilities that are in need of therapy including pediatric, behavioral health, hospitals, public schools, and senior care. PEDIATRIC CARESome of our pediatric care units include The Joshua House and Banyan Pediatrics. These monthly visits go to help 30-75 foster care children per visit in our community. The Banyan Pediatric is for kids with critical medical special needs that require medical supervision 24/7. The visits impact the emotional regulation and mental health of the patients and residents at these facilities.
